result:
REST: simple, cache-friendly, observable, broad tooling. Downsides: over/under-fetching, versioning friction, more endpoints/round trips.

GraphQL: client-shaped responses, fewer round trips, good for many clients with different data needs. Downsides: harder caching, auth, rate limits, N+1/perf traps, more server complexity.

Default: REST. Pick GraphQL when clients genuinely need flexible field selection across connected data.
